newsitem.title: USA: IBP acquires Bruss Co, a meat purveyor.
newsitem.headline: IBP acquires Bruss Co, a meat purveyor.

text.p: IBP Inc, the world's largest producer of fresh beef, pork and related products, said Wednesday it acquired The Bruss Co, a meat purveyor serving the domestic and international restaurant industry with annual revenues approaching $100 million.
IBP said the acquisition further expands its presence in the higher margin food service industry.
Terms of the deal were not disclosed.

Bruss processes and sells individual cuts of premium quality beef and pork to national accounts such as Outback Steakhouse. IBP's acquisition of Bruss follows its March 1997 acquisition of Foodbrands America Inc, a large U.S. producer, marketer and distributor of frozen and refrigerated products.

"Our acquisition of Foodbrands in March signaled an effort to pursue growth beyond our core fresh meats business," said Robert Peterson, chairman and chief executive officer of IBP. "Now, the addition of Bruss extends our reach into casual and fine dining restaurants and strengthens our position as a provider to the growing foodservice industry," he said in a statement.
Bruss, which employs about 200 people at its Chicago facility, will become a wholly-owned subsidiary of IBP. No changes in its operations are expected.
Shares of IBP were trading up 3/8 to 23-1/4.
